newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 17.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* Traders expect the market to experience a slight rebound after two days of consecutive losses and helped by the Central Bank's decision to lower the overnight borrowing rate.

* "We expect some gains on the rate cut news but it's still too early to see the real direction of the market since we still have to look at corporate earnings," said Jidgette Valenzuela, research manager at Lippo Securities.

* BPI Securities Corp said the equities market will remain weak until the currency situation stabilises. The brokerage firm said that if the next sell-off happens with bigger volumes, there may be a drop to the 2,450 support level.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index ended sharply lower for the second trading day, by 68.50 points at 2,587.36.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 63.17 points higher at 8,038.88. PLDT's ADR closed up $0/15 at $33 5/8.
* The Philippine peso ended at $29.30 to a dollar vs 29.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average remained at 32.1875 percent.
* The Central Bank said on Wednesday it would lower its overnight borrowing rate to 28 percent from 32 percent. The new rate will take effect on Thursday.
* President Fidel Ramos said there is no need to revise the country's economic targets for the year following the de facto devaluation of the peso.
* Philippine businessmen belonging to the Federation of Philippine Industries accused local banks of opportunism following last Friday's effective devaluation of the peso.

* Car prices in the Philippines were expected to rise after last week's de facto devaluation and most firms were waiting to see where the peso would settle before making their move, automobile manufacturers said.

* Marcopper Mining Corp said its board of directors approved the spin-off of its mining operations into a new, wholly-owned subsidiary. Marcopper will be converted into a holding company and its name will be changed to San Antonio Industrial Holdings.
* PLDT is planning to raise its long distance call rates possibly by September following the sharp depreciation of the peso.
* The Philippine property market is expected to weather the current foreign exchange turmoil and high interest rates, property experts said.

* The Philippine Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission have drafted rules to discourage backdoor listing. The bourse said trading of shares of a company that is the subject of backdoor listing will be automatically suspended and additional listings must comply with all rules covering initial public offering applications.
* Newspaper Today/Manila Bulletin said the Central Bank said the country's inflation rate could reach 8.5 percent "at most" due to the drop in the peso's value.
* The Philippine Star said quoting Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo that the government posted a budgetary surplus of 4.491 billion pesos for the first half of the year.
